market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1882 articles from Yahoo Finance, MarketBeat, simplywall.st, TradingView, Investing.com. The dominant theme is macro, with 805 macro items, 590 company items, 416 industry items, and 71 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
market_narrative: US equities have a constructive but selective bias as inflation, oil/energy, Fed/rates dominate the information flow. Before the open, the setup still needs confirmation from futures, Treasury yields, opening breadth and pre-market volume.
index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around inflation (244), Fed/rates (196), oil/energy (124), growth/jobs (21). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 374 positive, 182 negative, and 1326 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
